Hey goats, it's late and I should be getting some sleep before work but I just want to get some thoughts out of my head. I'm not really sure how to structure this so forgive me if I ramble. Also, I'm not trying to sound edgy/emo/deep or any bullshit like that. I have these thoughts and when I write them down I cringe a little because I know that's how they might come across, but I honestly don't mean for them to do so.

As a teenager & young 20 something, I wanted to "do something that made a difference" and to "have a cause". I think this is pretty normal and not just for young people. Unfortunately, there are more "important causes" in the world than there is time in the average human life, so it was clear to me that I'd have to focus my energies where I thought I could do most good.

Throughout this period I think I had a subconscious Utopian assumption: If only X then people would Y.

As time passed and I went through various life experiences, I started to become less starry-eyed and more disillusioned. (part of growing up I guess)

I began to come to the conclusion that people are not the victims of a problem, they ARE the problem. Any cause seeking to change some situation that people are in is ultimately misguided because people created this situation in the first place.

Basically, the world is as fucked up and shitty as it is because that's how people are. If you were able to restart reality from the beginning (if there is one/whatever that is) you'd still end up with a similar mess. (perhaps a "no shit!" statement)

It really struck me as obvious when I read a joke Onion article 3 years ago titled "Humanity Surprised It Still Hasn't Figured Out Better Alternative To Letting Power-Hungry Assholes Decide Everything".

I mean seriously, I feel like everything I hear in the news is just a repeat of a story arc we've seen over and over again in real life and the movies. All the corruption in our societal institutions and politics, all the injustices, all the cruelty and waste, everything wrong in the world is because of people.

I know referencing the Matrix is cliche and makes me sound like a 14 year old kid, but at the time I was coming to these realizations, it made me think of the scene where Morpheus is explaining to Neo how many people don't want to be unplugged, how they will fight you.

I came to the conclusion that the very people I wanted to help were actually part of the problem.

For example: Some of the causes I was really into for a while were things like privacy and democratizing technologies. I felt like technology was fundamentally changing the game with how power and the populace interact. If people had access to tools that could circumvent censorship and transfer more power from the ruling class to the ruled class, that was a good thing and would make the world a better place.

But really, the ruling class exists because the ruled class allows them to exist. I've slowly been coming to the realization that many people are fine with totalitarianism and dictatorship as long as some immediate comforts aren't infringed. "Look, seriously, if I'm able to lead a comfortable life in peace and pursue happiness, I don't give a fuck what some politicians or governments do." As long as people don't feel like something has an immediate "in your face" affect on them, it doesn't matter. It doesn't matter that everything you do is tracked, monitored, and stored to be used against you at some future date should the ruling powers wish. You don't immediately see the tracking and monitoring happening and in all likelihood nothing will ever happen, so really, who the fuck cares? (I find this appalling, but it seems to be the prevailing attitude)

Whatever. My problem is that now I feel like I don't really have any direction in my life. I have my job and some short term goals, but I don't really feel like there's a point. I tell myself "well, don't worry, sure the world's fucked, but just focus on yourself and enjoy the ride" but it just feels hollow.

In addition to that, I feel like I'm numb to any plight of my fellow man. Artwork doesn't really move me. I don't give a fuck about "expressions of the human experience" anymore because humans are dumb shits that create our own problems. I'm still entertained by art, but anything that's designed to emotionally grab me and make me care about another human just falls flat. I can still be interested, but instead of seeing some tragedy and thinking "omg, that's terrible!!!!" I think "well, that figures..." :(

I don't really like being this way. I'd like to have a purpose and to feel passion about something again.
Some nihilistic thoughts before I go to bed.

hello fellow coders. today im going to demonstrate a method to detect when a user has moved your app to the background (or stopped it entirely) and then run some code after a set amount of time, a task useful for things like idle timeouts.

for this demonstration we will be making a sample activity class, application class and service class. the application class will be used to hold a reference of the state of the app.. either "inFocus" or "outOfFocus". the activity will handle user interaction, toggle the state of the app in the application class, and launch our service. our service will contain a simple CountDownTimer to monitor idle activity, and any code we want to run after the timer reaches 0. lets get started.

lets get the annoying things out of the way first. open up your apps manifest and add lines to state your new classes:

<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
 package="com.myorg.myapp">
 <application
 android:name=".MyApplicationClass">
 <activity
 android:name=".MyActivity"/>
 <service
 android:name=".MyService"/>
 </application>
</manifest>

next lets define our application class. (side note.. if youre unfamiliar with the application class, its a useful place to perform a variety of tasks. in addition to being used by google analytics tools, its a good place to maintain static data about the current app instance without writing any data to disk). while it may be possible to launch multiple versions of any activity, there is only one application class running at any one time for any one android app.

public class MyApplicationClass extends Application {
 private static boolean FOCUSED = true;
 public static void appResumed() {
 FOCUSED = true;
 }

 public static void appPaused() {
 FOCUSED = false;
 }
 
 // ... this class is still useful for performing additional code execution if desired
}

easy enough right? the class maintains a static boolean variable to indicate if the app is in focus or not. additionally, there are three methods to return the app state and toggle the boolean variable to true and false.

then, lets set up our activity (these steps must be followed for ALL activities in your app. if you miss the onResume() override code, your timer will not stop running when that new activity is launched). the only work for the idle task is in the activity lifecycle callbacks onResume() and onPause().

public class MyActivity extends Activity {
 @Override
 public void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
 // do your activity business
 }
 
 @Override
 protected void onPause() {
 super.onPause();
 MyApplication.appPaused();
 Intent intent = new Intent(MyActivity.this, MyService.class);
 this.startService(intent);
 // additional onpause code can follow
 }
 
 @Override
 protected void onResume() {
 super.onResume();
 MyApplication.appResumed();
 Intent intent = new Intent(MyActivity.this, MyService.class);
 this.stopService(intent);
 // additional onresume code can follow
 }
}

no hassle or annoyances elsewhere in your activity. you can even make methods to perform those instructions to make your onPause and onResume look cleaner. your brain is probably already piecing together how all of this works, but lets knock out our service before we delve into specifics.

public class MyService extends Service {
 @Override
 public void onCreate() {
 // 1*60*1000 = 1 minute. can just as easily be written as 60000. letting the compiler do the multiplication is for readibility purposes as well as making it easier to quickly change the timer.
 CountDownTimer timer = new CountDownTimer(1 * 60 * 1000, 1000) { 
 @Override
 public void onTick(long millisUntilFinished) {
 if (MyApplication.isAppFocused()) {
 super.cancel();
 MyService.this.onDestroy();
 }
 }

 @Override
 public void onFinish() {
 if (!MyApplication.isAppFocused()){
 // the timer has counted down and app was not brought back into focus. perform your idle code here
 }
 MyService.this.onDestroy();
 }
 }.start(); 
 
 } 
}

so. what the hell is actually happening here? as i earler mentioned, our application class is just being used as a static placeholder for our app state. any time any activity is paused, the FOCUSED variable to toggled to false, our service gets launched, and our timer begins counting down. additionally, every time an activity is resumed, we have code to toggle FOCUSED back to true, which is picked up by our service's countdown timer in the onTick() method. this is why the timer doesn't keep counting down if you leave one activity and go to another, because the new activitys onResume() method is called immediately after the previous activitys onPause() method. however, if you leave your activity by pressing the home button for example, no onResume() method is called and the timer is allowed to reach 0. this is useful for a variety of reasons. idle timeouts/logouts, performing some tasks to precache some data, etc. i hope someone finds some use of this code, which was written with the support of the links listed below. lastly, to make things even easier, you could leave MyActivitys onCreate empty, and use MyActivity as a base class to be inherited from. So any time you make a new activity, have it extend MyActivity and all of the idle functionality are already included in onPause() and onResume()
